Thanks — quick technical callouts based on Amit's numbers and our internal perf models (attached inference-notes.pdf):

- For generate endpoint (avg 800 tokens / P95 2400): with continuous batching and prefix caching we can hit ~3k tokens/sec per A100-80GB instance for this family of model (quantized FP16 path). That suggests a pilot baseline of 2 instances to handle steady-state with headroom, and an autoscale policy to add 2 more during short 250 QPS bursts.
- For streaming (60 concurrent, 10-15m sessions): streaming cost is driven by concurrency rather than raw tokens/sec; recommend dedicating a small fleet of inference workers with low-latency kernels and warm KV cache handling. Practically, expect ~60-80 concurrent streams per 1 x A100 depending on batching window. If low jitter is critical, prefer single-tenant dedicated GPUs for streaming workers.
- Latency: meeting a 300ms P95 for streaming segment delivery requires aggressive batching tuning (sub-20ms batching windows) and a hot KV cache. We'll also need network egress sizing close to the service region.

Recommendation for pilot topology (high level):
- Option A (fastest to onboard): Hosted Redwood with reserved capacity for the pilot (2x A100 baseline + 2x burst) and a dedicated streaming pool (1x A100 dedicated for low-latency streams).
- Option B (enterprise control): Redwood Dedicated cluster (2x A100 baseline, streaming on a dedicated node) with private VPC for PHI controls. Slightly more setup time but more predictable latency and isolation.

I'll flesh out exact GPU SKU, expected tokens/sec numbers per node, and a cost delta between A100 vs H100 quantized path in the doc we will share by COB today.
